external_entities.name: reader
external_entities.description: A person who accesses the public site and fetches assets from the CDN.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Public site: readers hit the web server over HTTPS, some of them signed in.

external_entities.name: admin
external_entities.description: An administrator who maintains the database directly.
external_entities.source_excerpt: There is an admin who maintains the database directly rather than through the CMS.
external_entities.notes: The admin connects from wherever they happen to be; there is no jump host.

external_entities.name: CDN
external_entities.description: The CDN from which readers fetch images, stylesheets and downloads.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Readers fetch those from the CDN over HTTP.

processes.name: web server
processes.description: The web server hosting the public site and running the CMS.
processes.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS

processes.name: CMS
processes.description: The CMS running on the web server and maintaining pages, accounts and comments in the database.
processes.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS and keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database

data_stores.name: MySQL database
data_stores.description: The database containing pages, accounts and comments.
data_stores.source_excerpt: keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database
data_stores.notes: The description does not say whether the database is encrypted on disk.

data_stores.name: CDN bucket
data_stores.description: The CDN's bucket receiving newly published assets.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web server pushes them up to the CDN's bucket

data_flows.name: load site
data_flows.description: A reader accesses the public site through the web server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Public site: readers hit the web server over HTTPS
data_flows.notes: Some readers are signed in; the authentication mechanism is not stated.

data_flows.name: use site
data_flows.description: A reader uses the CMS-backed public site.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Public site: readers hit the web server over HTTPS, some of them signed in.
data_flows.notes: The CMS is the application running on the web server.

data_flows.name: keep content
data_flows.description: The CMS reads and writes pages, accounts and comments in the MySQL database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database

data_flows.name: fetch assets
data_flows.description: A reader fetches images, stylesheets and downloads from the CDN.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Readers fetch those from the CDN over HTTP.

data_flows.name: publish assets
data_flows.description: The web server pushes newly published assets to the CDN's bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When new assets are published the web server pushes them up to the CDN's bucket.
data_flows.notes: The source says nothing about how this push is authenticated.

data_flows.name: maintain database
data_flows.description: The admin directly maintains the MySQL database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: There is an admin who maintains the database directly rather than through the CMS.
data_flows.notes: The connection is unsecured, has no TLS, is straight to the box, and has no jump host.

trust_boundaries.name: hosted network
trust_boundaries.description: The hosted network containing the web server, CMS and MySQL database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS and keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database on the same hosted network.

assumptions.assumption: The web server is reachable from the internet because it serves the public site.
assumptions.basis: The source describes a public site whose readers hit the web server over HTTPS.

assumptions.assumption: The CDN bucket contains publicly available assets.
assumptions.basis: The assets are published and fetched by readers from the CDN.
